title: Customer Threads: Decision Braid — Rapid Synthesis & Tactical Requests
summary: Concise synthesis of customer feedback collected during Apr 2028 listening sprint. Emphasis on tactical fixes (<2w), medium bets (Q3), and one escalation needing exec alignment. This is a decision-oriented brief for product + eng partners.
request_clusters: Canary & rollout granularity — Ask: per-customer/canary routing and traffic mirroring with deterministic rollback. Quote: 'We need to test new model variants on 0.5% of our traffic but isolate any failures to a single customer key.' Impact hypothesis: reduces rollback blast radius and adoption latency. Quick fix (2w): add flagging in rollout UI to mark traffic by api-key and enable a 0.5/1/5% slider. Product bet (Q3): introduce traffic mirroring with shadow requests and automated metric diffing. Suggested owner: product-console + rollout-engineering. Estimate: low-med (UI+gateway changes).

Token-level cost visibility & cache telemetry — Ask: show token-level billing attribution and KV cache hit/miss rates per route. Quote: 'We can't explain cost spikes — is it cache miss or longer contexts?' Impact: improves cost optimization and simplifies customer troubleshooting. Quick fix (1-3w): surface recent per-route avg tokens and simple cache hit gauge in console. Product bet (Q3): expose per-request token breakdown via analytics API + alerting for sudden per-token cost regressions. Owner: observability + billing. Estimate: med.

Deterministic fallback semantics & quality alerts — Ask: explicit, explainable fallback policies (e.g., downrank to smaller model, degrade gracefully) and quality-regression alerts tied to prompt sets. Quote: 'When the large model is busy, we get garbage fallbacks and no signal that quality dropped.' Impact: prevents user-facing defects and reduces CS tickets. Quick fix (2w): document current fallback mapping and add opt-in stable-fallback toggle. Product bet (Q3): policy engine that evaluates rollback by quality metrics and auto-rolls based on guardrails. Owner: serving-runtime + product-hosted-api. Estimate: med-high.

Multi-region latency spikes & affinity routing — Ask: route to warm instances in-region and support client affinity to avoid cold-start tail latency. Quote: 'EU latency doubled after busy hours because traffic bounced between zones.' Impact: improves SLO adherence for enterprise customers. Quick fix (2-4w): recommend region pinning and add best-practice template for autoscaling thresholds. Product bet (Q4): proactive warm pools + predictive pre-warm based on traffic patterns. Owner: infra + sre. Estimate: high for full solution, quick wins achievable.

Embedding versioning & semantic-drift detection — Ask: clear embedding version metadata in responses + hooks for automatic reindexing and drift alerts. Quote: 'Our similarity search returned nonsense after a model update — we only found out after duplicates appeared.' Impact: reduces search regressions and reindexing costs. Quick fix (1-2w): append model_embedding_version header and a console list of embeddings versions per deployment. Product bet (Q3): automatic embedding drift monitor and one-click reindex pipeline. Owner: product-optimize + applied-ml. Estimate: med.

Billing transparency for partial responses & retries — Ask: prorated billing visibility when requests are retried or truncated; clearer docs about cost for streamed vs non-streamed tokens. Quote: 'We got billed for retries we didn't want; customers are asking for better predictability.' Impact: reduces billing disputes and churn. Quick fix (1-2w): publish a billing FAQ + example calculations and add retried-request flag in usage logs. Product bet (Q3): API param to opt into cost-protection (cap tokens charged per request) and webhook dispute automation. Owner: finance-and-legal + billing. Estimate: low-med.
decision_points: Approve small UI rollout slider for per-key canary percentage (product-console) — decision needed by 2028-04-25.
Prioritize token-level telemetry vs embedding-versioning for Q3 build allocation (product + eng) — vote in Roadmap sync 2028-04-22.
Executive approval for engineering effort to build warm-pool predictive pre-warming (infra budget spike) — exec ask by 2028-05-02.
next_steps: 1) Triage doc -> assign owners to each quick fix; owners to confirm plan by 2028-04-20.
2) Schedule 45m sync with product-console, observability, and serving-runtime to align on quick fixes (preferred: 2028-04-19).
3) Create minimal Jira tickets for each quick fix (CS to create, ENG to estimate) and link back to this doc.
4) Run two customer-validated tests for rollout slider with 3 pilot accounts (Marco to coordinate) by 2028-05-10.
5) If warm-pool exec approval obtained, scope Phase 1 that targets high-volume EU customers and estimate infra costs.
6) Publish a short CS-facing playbook with scripted responses for each cluster to reduce mean time to resolution.
notes: Context: feedback comes from 12 enterprise customers across payments, search, and conversational agents. Signals gathered via post-support interviews, in-product NPS prompts, and two customer advisory board sessions. Confidence levels: high for rollout/observability asks, medium for embedding drift, low-medium for billing feature requests (legal review required). Also: multiple customers requested a simpler way to opt out of automatic model upgrades — consider an "upgrade control" flag in Private and Dedicated offerings.

'Show me the cache hit rate for the last 24 hours — that's the first thing I want when costs go up.'
